text: Elvira produced eighty-one disciplinary canons — the largest body of legislation to survive from any pre-Nicene council — covering an unusually wide range of concerns: clerical discipline and conduct the treatment of Christians who had lapsed into idolatry under persecution marriage, including unions with pagans, Jews, and heretics usury, public entertainments, and pagan festivals penitential discipline for various grave sins Many of the penalties prescribed were severe by later standards: idolatry, repeated adultery, and certain other sins carried permanent exclusion from communion, even, in the case of Canon 1, at the point of death.
